prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters with simple rounded cartoon bodies, flat colour and black outlines, but every face is painted with startling real skin: pores, stubble, wrinkles, wet tired eyes, real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, no feature exaggerated. Every colour is laid on in thick visible oil brushstrokes. A grey winter afternoon in a 1930s schoolroom, the camera low along a row of tiny children's wooden desks: the lid of a little inkwell desk fills the near foreground. Just beyond it, large in frame and off-centre left, a heavy-set Black baker in his fifties in a vest and apron, shaved head, broken nose, double chin, squeezed into the tiny desk with his knees up round his chin, looking up with a real-skinned, worried face. Further along the row, other adults crammed in the same way: a young South Asian mother in a headscarf, a skinny old white dock worker in a flat cap. Small at the far end of the room, a plump teacher in her forties with round wire glasses, frizzy brown hair with a grey streak pinned in a bun and a brown cardigan points her long wooden pointer at a big blackboard wiped clean, dark and empty. Tall windows down the left wall let in cold blue-grey daylight with snow falling outside; a pot-bellied iron stove glows orange through its grille; one green-shaded lamp hangs over the teacher's desk. Worn floorboards wet from boots, puddles of melted snow, damp coats steaming on hooks. Most of the frame in shadow; the brightest values are the window light raking across the baker's face and the stove's orange glow. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
